data.title: Tallest Wooden Wind Turbine
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一家公司建造木制风力涡轮机塔，实现净零风能的可能性。传统风力涡轮机塔通常由钢材制成，而该公司采用木材，这种可再生材料不仅能减少碳排放，还能加速风能产业的可持续发展。文章强调了木制塔的创新性和环保优势，展示了其如何推动绿色能源的未来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风力发电实现净零排放的可行性及相关技术材料选择的问题

不同观点：
• **风力发电的净零排放是否为伪问题**：
  - [sebstefan] 认为风力发电的净零排放是一个由石油公司炮制出来的伪问题，依据是风力涡轮机的生命周期评估（包括制造、安装、维护和处置）显示其排放可以在运行5.3个月后抵消。
  - [exabrial] 也提出类似质疑，指出制造风力涡轮机的过程中会产生大量CO2，并质疑废旧碳纤维叶片的处理问题，但同时指出讨论这一问题往往被视为阴谋论。

• **材料选择与结构设计**：
  - [jbms] 认为钢材在强度上有优势，但提出空心设计的风力涡轮塔可以通过增加壁厚来提升强度，并提到Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL) 材料在强度重量比和成本上有优势，可能让塔更高。
  - [Bric3d] 指出风力涡轮的主要生态问题更多来自于叶片，而非塔身。
  - [svantana] 质疑风力涡轮塔为何采用空心圆筒设计，认为桁架结构可能提供更好的强度质量比。
  - [bjourne] 对用木材替代钢材的尝试持怀疑态度，指出历史上类似尝试多未成功，质疑此次有何不同。

• **成本与运输问题**：
  - [kieranmaine] 引用播客内容，指出风力涡轮机无法像太阳能和电池一样通过集装箱运输来降低成本，并提出是否能进一步缩小体积以降低成本的问题。
  - [jurschreuder] 指出风力涡轮机的能量消耗主要在混凝土基座而非钢材部分，并认为木制风力涡轮虽然可以建造但显得昂贵且劳动密集。

• **净零排放的具体含义**：
  - [aqme28] 对“净零”在此背景下的定义提出疑问，认为风力涡轮机应该是净负排放的，并质疑是否仅指材料和建设部分的净零。

补充讨论：
• **美学与情感因素**：
  - [rcpt] 表示喜欢风力涡轮机的外观，认为其代表未来，不理解为何有人对其有负面情绪。
  - [norome] 提出可以设计成旧式风车外观的风力涡轮机。

• **技术挑战与未来发展**：
  - [calmbonsai] 认为风力涡轮塔的建设并非当前业务模式中的重大挑战，质疑“净零”营销口号背后的数据支持，并指出叶片运输和组装问题仍未解决，认为这是未来发展的关键。

争议焦点：
• 风力发电的净零排放是否为伪问题以及废旧叶片的处理问题。
• 风力涡轮塔的材料选择与设计优化，特别是木材与钢材的对比。
• 风力涡轮机的运输成本与技术挑战，尤其是叶片设计与模块化问题。

data.title: Show HN: Lnk – Git-native dotfiles manager
data.author: yar-kravtsov
data.article_summary: "lnk" 是一个简化 dotfiles 管理的工具，通过将配置文件移至 `~/.config/lnk` 并创建符号链接回原位置，使用户能在原位置正常编辑和使用 Git 进行版本控制。它自动化了一些繁琐的步骤，如安全移动文件、创建相对符号链接、处理冲突等。用户可以通过简单的命令如 `lnk init`、`lnk add`、`lnk push` 和 `lnk pull` 来管理 dotfiles。相比其他工具，lnk 更加简约且无需复杂配置，支持单二进制文件，具有原子操作和跨平台的相对符号链接特性。当前版本为预发布状态，但作者日常使用稳定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：dotfiles 管理工具的功能、优缺点以及与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **pabs3** 提供了更多关于 dotfiles 资源的链接，供进一步参考。
• **efitz** 建议在使用 `lnk add` 添加文件时，检查文件中是否包含秘密信息，并在发现秘密信息时警告用户，需要使用 `--force` 来强制执行。
• **wanderingmind** 提出是否可以将 dot files 中的秘密加密并存储在远程，然后在拉取到本地时解密。
• **peterhadlaw** 质疑该工具与 GNU stow 的区别，询问其独特性。
• **m000** 指出大多数 dotfile 管理工具假设了一个统一的环境，这在不同设备上会导致问题，并列举了多个实例来说明这种情况。

补充讨论：
• **globular-toast** 认为 GNU stow 的多机器管理功能很糟糕，并提到 chezmoi 作为潜在的解决方案。
• **NicolaiS** 提供了一种使用 "git-dir" 选项克隆到子目录的方法，避免使用符号链接和污染 $HOME 目录。
• **nrvn** 分享了使用 "bare git at $HOMEDIR" 方法的经验，并列举了其优点和注意事项。
• **dmacvicar** 表示仅使用 git 和 GNU stow 管理 dotfiles 已经足够，并介绍了使用 GNU stow 的具体方法。
• **hk1337** 赞同使用 bare git 仓库的方法，认为符号链接和 GNU Stow 都很麻烦。
• **sam_lowry_** 描述了一种通过分支管理不同设备上 dotfiles 差异的方法。
• **dcre** 认为使用 git 和简单的 bash 脚本就可以实现相同功能，建议新手学习自己动手而不是依赖工具。
• **SuperCuber** 提到自己的项目 Dotter，认为其解决了不同设备上 dotfiles 差异的问题。
• **denysvitali** 比较了该工具与 Chezmoi，并对为什么 Chezmoi 会被认为过于复杂表示困惑。

争议焦点：
• dotfile 管理工具是否需要额外功能，还是仅使用 git 和简单脚本即可满足需求。
• 不同设备上 dotfiles 的管理复杂性以及如何有效解决这些差异。
• 符号链接和直接使用 git 仓库在 $HOME 中的优缺点。

How it works

After:  ~/.vimrc -> ~/.config/lnk/.vimrc (symlink)

data.title: Show HN: Rotary Phone Dial Linux Kernel Driver
data.author: sephalon
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个Linux内核驱动程序，能够将旋转拨号电话转换为一个evdev输入设备。通过此驱动，用户可以将传统的旋转拨号电话接入现代计算机系统，使其作为输入设备使用。项目遵循GNU通用公共许可证v2.0或更高版本，并于2025年1月1日创建。更多详细信息可参阅项目的README文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 rotary phone 及其技术改造的各种讨论，包括历史、技术实现、个人项目和遗憾。

不同观点：
• [anonymousiam] 分享了在1970年代末使用HP41C计算器制作旋转电话拨号器的经历，并提到与《HP-41C Synthetic Programming Manual》作者Keith Jarrett的偶遇。这一评论主要关注历史技术创新和个人项目。
• [jtwaleson] 提到将旋转电话转换为蓝牙耳机，并提供了相关项目链接。这一评论侧重于现代技术与传统设备的结合。
• [mauvehaus] 提出将旋转拨号引入iPhone的设想，但被拒绝。评论表达了对过去机会错失的遗憾。
• [tempodox] 对[jtwaleson]的评论做出回应，更关注于Linux系统的实用功能，如Bluetooth音频和UTF-8支持。

data.title: The legacy of the iconic Nakagin capsule tower
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: MoMA将于2025年7月10日至2026年7月12日举办展览《中银胶囊塔的多元生命》，重现这座于1972年在东京银座建成、2022年被拆除的标志性建筑。该塔是日本新陈代谢派建筑运动的代表作，旨在体现自然生长和转变。展览展示了一个完全修复的胶囊单元A1305以及四十多件档案材料，包括模型、宣传单、影片和访谈，揭示这些微型单元如何适应超越最初设计目的的生活方式。通过这个回顾展，MoMA探讨了在不断更新的城市中保存建筑概念的意义。展览还将推出一本由Kotsioris撰写的对应书籍，并与日本协会合作举办一系列活动，以连接该项目在其原背景和美国新观众中的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Metabolism运动及其代表性建筑Nakagin Capsule Tower的讨论，涉及历史、建筑设计理念、实际维护问题以及文化差异等。

不同观点：
• [aabhay] 认为Metabolism运动旨在创建模块化和动态的建筑及城市规划，能够有效部署、迁移和再利用。他提到该运动的成员设计了从东京标志性电话亭到酱油瓶，再到滑雪小屋，甚至包括填海造陆的全套城市设计方案。

• [Incipient] 担心类似高塔建筑的维护问题，特别是由于复杂的几何结构和外部密封要求，在潮湿环境下可能导致建筑老化过快，维护成本高昂，可能不值得修复。

• [UI_at_80x24] 将这种建筑美学与威廉·吉布森的《神经漫游者》以及《银翼杀手》等作品中的黑暗、工业风格相联系，认为这些作品出现在相近的年代，并相互提供了灵感。

• [Luc] 提供了更多内部照片的链接，为讨论提供了视觉参考。

• [user_7832] 希望看到更多类似概念的探索，认为应在“完全模块化”和“完全静态建筑”之间找到平衡，并指出资金和拆除现有建筑物的难度是推广此类项目的障碍。

• [a1o] 对相关建筑摄影书籍表示兴趣，询问是否存在专门关于Nakagin Capsule Tower的摄影集。

• [pvg] 提供了一个2021年的相关讨论链接，引导读者查看更多背景信息。

• [morkalork] 开玩笑地提到《龙珠》中的“胶囊公司”可能参考了Metabolism运动的理念，因为两者在名称和未来主义风格上有相似之处。

• [ginko] 质疑在欧洲城市是否能拆除像Nakagin Capsule Tower这样的建筑，认为可能会受到城市保护主义者的干预。

• [os2warpman] 指出Nakagin Capsule Tower尽管受到艺术家和设计师的赞誉，但由于入住率低而年久失修，认为人们并不愿意住在这样酷但狭小的空间中，即使是作为度假屋。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Nakagin Capsule Tower的实际可行性和居住舒适度。一方面，其设计理念和美学价值受到赞赏；另一方面，实际维护和居住体验存在问题。

• 文化差异：[ginko] 提到在欧洲城市可能面临的保护主义问题，反映了不同文化背景下对历史建筑保护的不同态度。

• 经济因素：[user_7832] 提到资金和拆除成本是推广此类项目的障碍，讨论了经济因素对建筑设计和城市规划的影响。

an Architectural Time Capsule revisited in new york
The
Nakagin Capsule Tower
returns to public view this summer in a new light, as
MoMA
in New York opens an exhibition centered on its half-century lifespan. Built in
Tokyo
’s Ginza district in 1972 and dismantled in 2022, the structure was once among the clearest architectural expressions of
Metabolism
in
Japan
, a movement that sought to mirror natural growth and transformation in the built environment. Now, through a single, fully restored capsule and a constellation of archival materials, MoMA reactivates that legacy with the goal of inspiring inquiry over nostalgia.
Presented in the exhibition is capsule A1305, originally situated on the uppermost floor. For its display, it has been returned to near-original condition. Fragments of other salvaged units complete the restoration, from its modular furnishings to the audio controls and Sony color TV that defined its compact domesticity. Surrounding the capsule are more than 40 materials drawn from the tower’s five-decade history — models, promotional leaflets, film reels, and interviews that reveal how these micro-units adapted to lives far beyond their initial purpose. In a city shaped by constant renewal, this retrospective probes what it means to preserve an architectural concept.
The Many Lives of the Nakagin Capsule Tower will be on view at MoMA from July 10th, 2025 until July 12th, 2026.
Kishō Kurokawa in front of the completed Nakagin Capsule Tower, 1974. image by Tomio Ohashi
kishō Kurokawa’s Unfolding Vision
MoMA is set to exhibit The Many Lives of the Nakagin Capsule Tower as an investigation into the iconic structure, which was originally imagined by architect Kishō Kurokawa as a machine for living that could regenerate itself. While the concrete towers were to remain as infrastructural anchors, the capsules were intended to be swapped out as needs evolved. That replacement never came. Yet the life of the tower defied stillness. The
museum
’s curatorial team, led by Evangelos Kotsioris and Paula Vilaplana de Miguel, foregrounds the tower’s informal transformations — capsules turned into galleries, DJ booths, or quiet spaces of solitude — offering a portrait of architecture shaped by use that transcends its intended programming.
By acquiring capsule A1305 in 2023, MoMA ensured a rare physical survival of a building long dismissed as unmaintainable. It is one of just fourteen capsules worldwide to have been carefully reassembled in original form. Visitors will be able to experience the unit in full during selected member activations, reinforcing the tower’s original intent as a space to be inhabited. The Nakagin Capsule Tower’s presence at MoMA sits within the museum’s wider ambition to question permanence, authorship, and the mutable nature of design.
Kisho Kurokawa, Architect & Associates (Tokyo, est. 1962). Nakagin Capsule Tower, Tokyo. 1970–72. exterior view. 1972. image by Tomio Ohashi
Extending the Conversation around nakagin capsule tower
MoMA’s exhibition The Many Lives of the Nakagin Capsule Tower will extend beyond the gallery. A companion book authored by Kotsioris for the MoMA One on One series explores the structure’s life cycle, from its speculative roots to its final days. With rarely published documents and firsthand accounts from the building’s last residents, the volume deepens the narrative around this experimental habitat. A suite of programs in partnership with Japan Society will also unfold throughout the exhibition’s yearlong run, framing the project within both its original context and its new American audience.
night time at the Nakagin Capsule Tower, with Mr. Takayuki Sekine seen through the window of capsule B1004, 2016. image © Jeremie Souteyrat
Kisho Kurokawa, Architect & Associates (Tokyo, est. 1962). Capsule A1305 from the Nakagin Capsule Tower. 1970–72; restored 2022–23. Steel, wood, paint, plastics, cloth, polyurethane, glass, ceramic, and electronics, 8′ 4 3/8″ × 8′ 10 5/16″ × 13′ 10 9/16″ (255 × 270 ×423 cm). The Museum of Modern Art, New York. Gift of Jo Carole and Ronald S. Lauder, Alice and Tom Tisch, and the Nakagin Capsule Tower Preservation and Restoration Project, Tokyo

data.title: The Xenon Death Flash: How a Camera Nearly Killed the Raspberry Pi 2
data.author: DamonHD
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了2015年Raspberry Pi 2被发现的一个罕见硬件漏洞：被氙气闪光灯照射时会立即关机。用户Peter Onion在论坛上报告了这一现象，引发社区广泛讨论和实验，最终确定问题是由于U16电源调节芯片采用了裸露的晶圆级芯片封装（WL-CSP），高强度光照引发光电效应，导致芯片电压调节异常。尽管临时解决方案是用Blu-Tack遮盖芯片，但长期解决方案是改进设计以防止类似问题。这一事件揭示了现代电子产品在追求小型化过程中对光学干扰的脆弱性，并提醒工程师在设计中考虑此类风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WLCSP部件的光敏性问题及其在工程设计中的处理

不同观点：
• K0balt认为，WLCSP部件的光敏性并不是社区新发现的，数据手册中早已明确指出，且这是硅芯片的基本特性。他批评那些不阅读数据手册的工程师，并指出这是基本的工程责任。
• skrebbel对文章的写作风格提出批评，认为文章添加了许多不相关的信息，并且有过度渲染的倾向，建议减少对LLM（语言模型）的依赖。
• itishappy指出半导体效应通常是可逆的，并讨论了光电效应在半导体中的应用，提到通过高强度光可以刺激芯片中的结点，但实际操作中效率较低。
• geerlingguy提到不同版本的Raspberry Pi存在的硬件问题，并推测未来Pi 6可能会出现新的硬件 quirks。

补充讨论：
• nickdothutton分享了关于芯片封装中放射性杂质导致SPARC CPU缓存损坏的经历。
• rini17提到透明助听器罩在阳光下会导致噪音的问题。
• pvg提供了相关的HN讨论线程链接。
• RajT88描述了在航空母舰上使用DV摄像机时遇到雷达干扰的问题，并通过物理遮挡解决。
• pclmulqdq解释了后硅调试中使用激光照射芯片的操作及其光敏性问题。
• xeonmc讨论了光强度和波长对硅芯片的影响，指出需要特定带隙能量才能触发故障。
• prpl分享了使用氙气闪光校准延迟的经验。
• tallanvor回忆了AT&T展示数字交换技术时因闪光导致EEPROM崩溃的故事。
• johnea分享了20世纪80年代使用紫外可擦除微控制器时被闪光干扰的经历。

争议焦点：
• K0balt与潜在的未充分阅读数据手册的工程师之间的观点对立，一方认为这是基本工程知识，另一方可能忽视了这些细节。
• skrebbel对文章写作风格和LLM使用上的批评，与其他技术讨论形成对比，显示出对文章呈现方式的不同期望。

44080533.article_content:
The Raspberry Pi 2’s vulnerability to xenon flashes became one of the most unusual hardware bugs in computing history.
Table of Contents
The Community Detective Story Begins
The Hunt for the Vulnerable Component
The Physics Behind the “Xenon Death Flash”
This Wasn’t Actually Unprecedented
The Fixes: From Blu-Tack to Better Design
What This Revealed About Modern Electronics
The Legacy of an “Adorable Bug”
Lessons for Today’s Connected World
I’ve seen plenty of weird computer bugs in my time, but nothing quite like what Peter Onion discovered in February 2015. He was proudly photographing his brand new Raspberry Pi 2 when something bizarre happenedâevery time his camera flash went off, his Pi instantly powered down.
At first, Peter thought it was just a coincidence. But after it happened three times in a row, he realized he’d stumbled onto something unprecedented.
His post to the Raspberry Pi forums
with the innocent title “Why is the PI2 camera-shy?” would soon reveal one of the strangest hardware vulnerabilities in modern computing history.
The Community Detective Story Begins
#
Peter Onion wasn’t just any userâhe was a veteran of the Raspberry Pi community and a regular at Raspberry Jams in Cambridge and Bletchley. When he reported that
taking flash photos caused his Pi 2 to crash
, the community took notice.
What happened next was like watching a crowd-sourced CSI episode unfold in real time. Forum users immediately began experimenting with different cameras and light sources. User “jdb” made a crucial discovery: his Samsung Note2 with LED flash caused no problems, but his Samsung K Zoom with a xenon flash reliably crashed the Pi 2.
This distinction between LED and xenon technology became the first major clue. The community had found their smoking gunâbut they still needed to figure out why.
The Hunt for the Vulnerable Component
#
The real detective work began when users started systematically testing which part of the Pi 2 was actually vulnerable. The initial assumption was that the main processor chip might be the culprit, but covering it with a blob of Blu-Tack (yes, really) didn’t solve the problem.
Then someone tried flipping the Pi upside down. Suddenly, it was immune to flash photography. This proved the vulnerability was purely opticalâlight had to physically reach a specific component on the board.
Through methodical testing,
the community isolated the problem to the U16 chip
âa small power supply regulator located between the USB connector and HDMI port. When they covered just this tiny component with Blu-Tack, the crashes stopped completely.
But what made this particular chip so sensitive to light?
The Physics Behind the “Xenon Death Flash”
#
The answer lay in modern semiconductor packaging. The U16 chip used something called Wafer-Level Chip Scale Packaging (WL-CSP), which is exactly what it sounds likeâ
a bare silicon die with solder balls attached directly to the circuit board
. Unlike traditional chips that are fully encapsulated in opaque plastic, WL-CSP chips prioritize miniaturization over protection.
This exposed silicon became the Pi 2’s Achilles’ heel. When hit by high-intensity light, the photoelectric effect kicked inâthe same phenomenon Einstein won a Nobel Prize for explaining.
High-energy photons striking the semiconductor created unexpected electron flows
, disrupting the voltage regulation circuitry and causing an immediate shutdown.
The intensity threshold was crucial. Regular LED camera flashes didn’t produce enough photons, but xenon flashes and laser pointers packed sufficient punch to trigger the malfunction. Even more interesting, the effect required silicon’s specific bandgap energyâmeaning infrared and visible light could potentially cause problems, but only at extreme intensities.
This Wasn’t Actually Unprecedented

While the Raspberry Pi incident captured headlines, similar optical interference problems had been lurking in the semiconductor industry for years.
An engineer at EDN Network revealed
that his company had encountered the exact same issue twelve years earlier with a CSP amplifier for a cell phone prototype. The phone’s own camera flash would cause the amplifier to spike when light penetrated the chip packaging.
Even more dramatic was a 1997 incident at the Haddam Neck nuclear plant in Connecticut.
A training department member took a flash photograph of a fire detection panel

These incidents revealed a broader truth: as semiconductors became smaller and more exposed, they also became more vulnerable to optical interference that traditional testing never considered.

data.author: yoeven
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了小语言模型定义的变化。过去，小模型可能只有几百万参数，能在手机或笔记本上运行，而如今，拥有300亿参数但只需一个GPU运行的模型也被称为“小模型”。到2025年，小模型主要分为两类：边缘优化模型（如Phi-3-mini和Gemma 2B，适合移动设备）和GPU友好模型（如Llama 3 70B，可在单个GPU上运行）。小模型的优势在于其专门化，能够在特定任务上超越通用大模型。如今，“小”更多指的是模型的可部署性、单GPU运行能力和易于调优的特性，而不仅仅是参数大小。小模型在成本和隐私方面具有重要意义，正在改变AI应用的格局。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同背景下“小型语言模型”的定义和分类

不同观点：
• **antirez**：根据模型运行所需的硬件资源和参数规模，将模型分为非常小、小、中、大、超大等类别。例如，非常小的模型可以在Raspberry Pi等边缘设备上运行，而超大模型则是如Gemini 2.5 PRO等最先进的大型模型。

• **zellyn**：以能运行在高端MacBook Pro上为分界线，认为接近这种大小的模型已经能执行如编码等任务。

• **armcat**：指出“小型语言模型”的定义随时间变化。过去的大型模型如BERT（1.1亿参数）在2018年被视为大型，而如今小型LLM的参数范围在3-4B左右。

• **Havoc**：认为模型大小的划分有些 arbitrary，提出以能否在3090显卡上运行为合理的分界线。

• **breckinloggins**：建议借用旧DOS内存模型的命名方式，根据运行设备的能力定义模型大小级别，如“tiny”可在微控制器上运行，“compact”可在Raspberry Pi上运行等。

• **mcswell**：质疑“小型模型”的定义，指出如果训练成本高达1万美元，是否还能算作小型模型。并提到一些小于1B参数的模型在特定任务中的应用。

• **srikz**：希望看到能在浏览器中通过WebAssembly运行的模型，理想大小在100MB以下。

• **nickpsecurity**：认为术语“小型模型”过于泛化，建议以能否在24小时内用一台A100 GPU完成训练为标准定义模型大小，并提到一些在10M-200M参数范围内的模型。

• **rickstanley**：提出是否可以有模型推荐其他适合特定机器配置的模型，例如基于Ryzen 9 6000S和RTX 3060m的笔记本电脑。

• **alexpham14**：赞赏根据实际影响和可部署性来定义“小型”模型，而不是单纯依赖参数数量。

• **GolDDranks**：认为传统Markov模型是小型语言模型的代表。

• **Dwedit**：提到“BabyLlama”模型，其参数规模在百万级别而非十亿级别。

• **stephantul**：质疑原帖是否完全由GPT-4o生成。

• **KasianFranks**：指出混合专家模型（MoE）在结合小型和大型语言模型的优势。

• **croes**：质疑大型语言模型如何能同时是小型语言模型，反映出定义上的困惑。

补充讨论：
- 模型大小的定义随时间、硬件能力和应用场景的变化而变化。
- 训练成本和模型推荐系统成为讨论中的关注点。
- 对小型模型的实际应用场景，如在浏览器中运行，提出了具体期望。
- 不同术语和分类方法的相对性和适用性引起争议。

44048751.article_content:
What Even Is a Small Language Model Now?
15 May 2025
Yoeven D Khemlani
Share this article
If you asked someone in 2018 what a "small model" was, they'd probably say something with a few million parameters that ran on a Raspberry Pi or your phone. Fast-forward to today, and we're calling 30B parameter models "small"—because they
only
need one GPU to run.
So yeah, the definition of "small" has changed.
Small Used to Mean... Actually Small
Back in the early days of machine learning, a "small model" might've been a decision tree or a basic neural net that could run on a laptop CPU. Think scikit-learn, not LLMs.
Then came transformers and large language models (LLMs). As these got bigger and better, anything not requiring a cluster of A100s suddenly started to feel... small by comparison.
Today, small is more about
how deployable
the model is, not just its size on paper.
Types of Small Models (By 2025 Standards)
We now have two main flavors of small language models:
1. Edge-Optimized Models
These are the kind of models you can run on mobile devices or edge hardware. They're optimized for speed, low memory, and offline use.
Examples
: Phi-3-mini (3.8B), Gemma 2B, TinyLlama (1.1B)
Use cases
: voice assistants, translation on phones, offline summarization, chatbots embedded in apps
2. GPU-Friendly Models
These still require a GPU, but just
one GPU
—not a whole rack. In this category, even 30B or 70B models can qualify as "small".
Examples
: Meta Llama 3 70B (quantized), MPT-30B
Use cases
: internal RAG pipelines, chatbot endpoints, summarizers, code assistants
The fact that you can now run a 70B model on a single 4090 and get decent throughput? That would've been science fiction a few years ago.
Specialization: The Real Power Move
One big strength of small models is that they don't need to do everything. Unlike GPT-4 or Claude that try to be general-purpose brains, small models are often
narrow and optimized
.
That gives them a few key advantages:
They stay lean
— no need to carry weights for tasks they’ll never do.
They’re more accurate in-domain
— a small legal model will outperform a general-purpose LLM on legal docs.
They’re easier to fine-tune
— less data, faster iteration.
Small models shine when you know what you want. Think: summarizing medical records, identifying security vulnerabilities, parsing invoices—stuff that doesn't need general reasoning across the internet.
30B+ Models: Still Small?
Sounds weird, but yes. The bar for what’s considered "small" keeps shifting.
With the right quantization and engineering, even a 70B model can run comfortably on a high-end consumer GPU:
Llama 3.1 70B
can be shrunk from 140GB (FP16) to 21GB (2-bit), running on a single 24GB VRAM card.
Throughput? ~60 tokens/sec — totally usable for many production workloads.
So now we talk about models being "small" if they’re:
Deployable without distributed inference
Runnable on one GPU (especially consumer-grade)
Tunable without a lab full of TPUs
It’s less about size, more about
practicality
.
Everyday Small Models: The Unsung Heroes
Not all small models are new. Some of the most widely used models today have been around for years, quietly powering everyday tools we rely on.
Google Translate
: Since 2006, it's been translating billions of words daily. In 2016, Google switched to a neural machine translation system, GNMT, which uses an encoder-decoder architecture with long short-term memory (LSTM) layers and attention mechanisms. This system, with over 160 million parameters, significantly improved translation fluency and accuracy.
AWS Textract
: This service extracts text and data from scanned documents. It's been a staple in automating document processing workflows, handling everything from invoices to medical records.
These models may not be cutting-edge by today's standards, but they've been instrumental in shaping the AI landscape and continue to serve millions daily.
Why This Matters
Small models are becoming a huge deal:
Startups
can deploy LLMs without spending six figures on infra.
Developers
can run local models for privacy-focused apps.
Enterprises
can fine-tune task-specific LLMs without massive overhead.
And when a "small model" can hold its own against GPT-3.5 in benchmarks? The game has officially changed.
TL;DR
Small models used to mean tiny. Now they mean "runs without drama."
You’ve got edge models, GPU-ready models, and everything in between.
Specialization is where small models shine.
30B and 70B models can be small—if they’re optimized well.
Practicality > parameter count.
In a world chasing ever-bigger models, small ones are quietly doing more with less—and that's exactly what makes them powerful.

The Evening was
small in the shadow of the other boats. When I arrived at the dock, it was well past midnight, and a misty rain was falling—the edge of a storm far out at sea. Mick, the captain, was blunt and salty; not old, but weathered. He led me on board and pointed down the ladder to the hull, where I immediately got into bed and fell asleep. When I woke up, Mick had gone into town, and I began to look around in the mute light of the overcast morning.
Explore the June 2025 Issue
Check out more from this issue and find your next story to read.
View More
Our plan that October was to fish for albacore off the coast of Washington State. These would be short trips—four or five days at a time—to train me up for the summer, when I’d join Mick for a real voyage. I’d taken a Coast Guard course at a community college and had my Merchant Mariner certificate, but I’d never worked on a fishing boat before. In the daylight, the Evening looked ramshackle, as if it had survived 80 years in the northern Pacific more by luck than design. I found a few photos of Mick’s family, and the Evening’s Coast Guard certificate. “Constructed 1941, 43 feet, commercial (uninspected).” On deck, fishing lines were tangled with seaweed. Scattered everywhere were about a dozen rubber doormats stamped with the words
Thankful, Grateful, and Blessed
. On a workbench stood a statue of the Virgin Mary.
We spent a few days waiting for the weather to clear. Mick did paperwork and chores and I tidied the boat. One day we took the catch he had stored in the hold’s briny ice to a cannery on a spit of land between the ocean and Grays Harbor. Water from the Chehalis River flowed into the harbor, forming a standing wave where the two bodies met. I watched a ship leaving the harbor. When it crossed the river bar, it pitched and rolled. Mick and I would be taking the same route in a few days, but the Evening was half the size of that ship, old, and made of wood. The wave looked large enough to swallow us.
That afternoon, Mick suggested that we “take her out for a little spin.” Days of stormy weather had turned the water brown. Bobbing under the surface, barely visible, were entire trees that had washed down the Chehalis. Mick made sure I knew how to use the radio, and reminded me that the Coast Guard was on Channel 16. He pointed out the white canister on one wall that held the emergency radio beacon, which would go off automatically if submerged. The life raft, he explained, would release on its own.
The forecast finally showed minimal wind, minimal swell. We’d leave Thursday, October 12, 2023, and be back Sunday or Monday. On Wednesday night, I went out for a cheeseburger and called my mom. When she asked if I was excited, I said yes.
My parents thought
I was throwing my life away. I was 27, and since graduating from the University of Virginia five years earlier, I’d been living in California, where I spent my time working at the counter of a surf shop, running cocktails to tourists on the ferry to Catalina Island, and surfing. In college, I’d talked about going to law school, or taking the Foreign Service exam. But as graduation approached, I began to look down the line at the rest of my life, and I knew I didn’t want that kind of career. I wasn’t sure I wanted any career at all.
I’d read
East of Eden
and
Barbarian Days
, and imagined California as a place where I could get far away from my East Coast upbringing, the collar-and-tie of my Episcopal-school childhood. I didn’t break the news to my parents until a week before my departure.
From the April 2025 issue: Graydon Carter on how six months working on the railroad changed his life
They said I hadn’t thought it through, that it didn’t sound like I had a plan. The lack of a plan was the point, I told them: “I’ll bus tables or whatever—I can find a job when I get there.” I could tell they thought the whole thing was ridiculous. In the end, I blew up at them. I told them I didn’t want the life they had chosen for me. I told them that they didn’t understand me, that I hadn’t asked for and didn’t want the blessings they’d given me.
After I left, I’d call home about once a month. They’d ask how I was doing; I’d tell them I was “figuring things out just fine.”
I bounced around—San Diego, Santa Cruz, Newport Beach—making friends and surfing as much as possible: daily, twice daily, sometimes all day long. But by the summer of 2023, I was restless. I would never have admitted it to my parents, but my job at the surf shop was getting old. Even surfing itself was beginning to feel rote—the same breaks, the same people, the same wave.
I wanted to get out of California, at least for a little while. I’d go to Australia for a year-long surfing bender. Maybe I’d meet some Australian girl—no, I definitely would—and never come back. I got a work visa. All I needed was

data.title: DumPy: NumPy except it's OK if you're dum
data.author: RebelPotato
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了NumPy在处理高维数组时的复杂性问题，并提出了一种简化的解决方案，称为"DumPy"。作者认为NumPy虽然强大，但需要用户进行过多思考，尤其是在处理数组维度时，不同函数有不同的规则，导致使用不便。作者建议回归使用类似循环和索引的语法，但实际上仍将其编译为向量化操作，从而避免手动循环的低效问题。这种方法旨在减少不必要的思考，同时保持运算速度，特别是针对GPU的优化。文章通过具体例子展示了NumPy的复杂性以及DumPy的简化潜力，强调简单直观的操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Numpy的语法和使用难度，以及是否有更好的替代方案或改进方式。

不同观点：
• [the__alchemist] 认为Numpy的语法难以理解，尤其在嵌套循环和Numpy函数的对比中，嵌套循环更易理解和通用。
• [jampekka] 部分同意上述观点，但强调Numpy的广播机制使其强大和灵活，尽管广播规则可以更简单一致。同时指出使用vmap和FP在Python中受限。
• [turtletontine] 提出Numpy的einsum函数可以实现类似的功能，尽管接口不同，但也能简化复杂操作。
• [credit_guy] 不认为 loops 是好的解决方案，指出常规Numpy虽然复杂但可以处理任意形状的数组，并分享了自己使用Copilot进行向量化的经验。
• [joshjob42] 倾向使用Julia，因为其在矩阵运算和GPU支持上更优秀，并且可以通过PyCall调用Python库。
• [Gimpei] 强调高维数组操作本身就难以理解，Numpy可能可以改进，但loops不是解决方案，且Numpy语法不易读。
• [bee_rider] 对广播机制持批评态度，认为如果Numpy没有广播可能会更好，并指出某些操作应返回错误而非执行不相关操作。

补充讨论：
• [mpascale00] 希望有类似`ggplot2`的直观语法用于高维操作，并认为可以改进使数学运算更符合Python的Zen。
• [kevmo314] 对loops提案不认同，提到TensorFlow的懒惰求值导致调试困难，认为PyTorch因此胜出，并表示理解对Numpy的挫败感。
• [okigan] 认同文章中对Numpy使用中WTF时刻的解释，尽管自己不常使用Numpy。
• [bbminner] 支持新的索引和广播表示方式，并提到这种表示可能允许找到更优的低级实现，同时提到曾见过相关研究但未能找到引用。
• [shiandow] 对新语法的未来适应性表示担忧，询问是否需要持续开发以保持更新，并提出一些替代语法建议。
• [3eb7988a1663] 仅对代码字体颜色提出小抱怨。
• [duchenne] 希望Pytorch能有类似改进。
• [netbioserror] 认为这种DSL构造适合有宏的语言，如Lisp、Nim，并讨论高维数组索引和广播的理想语法。

争议焦点：
• Numpy广播机制的优缺点：部分用户认为广播使Numpy强大灵活，另一些用户则认为广播导致不必要的复杂性和错误。
• 使用loops还是Numpy函数：部分用户认为嵌套循环更易理解和通用，但其他用户指出处理高维数组时loops并不实际。

What I want from an array language is:
Don’t make me think.
Run fast on GPUs.
Really, do not make me think.
Do
not
.
I say NumPy misses on three of these. So I’d like to propose a “fix” that—I claim—eliminates 90% of unnecessary thinking, with no loss of power. It would also fix all the things based on NumPy, for example every machine learning library.
I know that sounds grandiose. Quite possibly you’re thinking that good-old dynomight has finally lost it. So I warn you now: My solution is utterly non-clever. If anything is clever here, it’s my single-minded rejection of cleverness.
To motivate the fix, let me give my story for how NumPy went wrong. It started as a nice little library for array operations and linear algebra. When everything has two or fewer dimensions, it’s great. But at some point, someone showed up with some higher-dimensional arrays. If loops were fast in Python, NumPy would have said, “Hello person with ≥3 dimensions, please call my ≤2 dimensional functions in a loop so I can stay nice and simple, xox, NumPy.”
But since loops are slow, NumPy instead took all the complexity that would
usually
be addressed with loops and pushed it down into individual functions. I think this was a disaster, because
every time
you see some function call like
np.func(A,B)
, you have to think:
OK, what shapes do all those arrays have?
And what does
np.func
do when it sees those shapes?
Different functions have different rules. Sometimes they’re bewildering. This means constantly thinking and constantly moving dimensions around to appease the whims of particular functions. It’s the
functions
that should be appeasing
your
whims!
Even simple-looking things like
A*B
or
A[B,C]
do quite different things depending on the starting shapes. And those starting shapes are often themselves the output of
previous
functions, so the complexity spirals.
Worst of all, if you write a new ≤2 dimensional function, then high-dimensional arrays are your problem.
You
need to decide what rules to obey, and then
you
need to re-write your function in a much more complex way to—
Voice from the back
: Python sucks! If you used a real language, loops would be fast! This problem is stupid!
That was a strong argument, ten years ago. But now everything is GPU, and GPUs hate loops. Today, array packages are cheerful interfaces that
look
like Python (or whatever) but are actually embedded languages that secretly compile everything into special GPU instructions that run on whole arrays in parallel. With big arrays, you need GPUs. So I think the speed of the host language doesn’t matter so much anymore.
Python’s slowness may have paradoxically turned out to be an
advantage
, since it forced everything to be designed to work without loops even before GPUs took over.
Still, thinking is bad, and NumPy makes me think, so
I don’t like NumPy
.
So what’s the fix?
Here’s my extremely non-clever idea: Let’s just admit that loops were better. In high dimensions, no one has yet come up with a notation that beats loops and indices. So, let’s do this:
Bring back the syntax of loops and indices.
But don’t actually
execute
the loops. Just take the syntax and secretly compile it into vectorized operations.
Also, let’s get rid of all the insanity that’s been added to NumPy because loops were slow.
That’s basically the whole idea. If you take those three bullet-points, you could probably re-derive everything I do below. I told you this wasn’t clever.

44080181.article_summary: 文章讨论了NumPy在处理高维数组时的复杂性问题，并提出了一种简化的解决方案，称为"DumPy"。作者认为NumPy虽然强大，但需要用户进行过多思考，尤其是在处理数组维度时，不同函数有不同的规则，导致使用不便。作者建议回归使用类似循环和索引的语法，但实际上仍将其编译为向量化操作，从而避免手动循环的低效问题。这种方法旨在减少不必要的思考，同时保持运算速度，特别是针对GPU的优化。文章通过具体例子展示了NumPy的复杂性以及DumPy的简化潜力，强调简单直观的操作。

F2 - Command-Line Batch Renaming
F2
is a cross-platform command-line tool for batch renaming files and
directories
quickly
and
safely
. Written in Go!
What does F2 do differently?
Compared to other renaming tools, F2 offers several key advantages:
Dry Run by Default
: It defaults to a dry run so that you can review the
renaming changes before proceeding.
Variable Support
: F2 allows you to use file attributes, such as EXIF data
for images or ID3 tags for audio files, to give you maximum flexibility in
renaming.
Comprehensive Options
: Whether it's simple string replacements or complex
regular expressions, F2 provides a full range of renaming capabilities.
Safety First
: It prioritizes accuracy by ensuring every renaming operation
is conflict-free and error-proof through rigorous checks.
Conflict Resolution
: Each renaming operation is validated before execution
and detected conflicts can be automatically resolved.
High Performance
: F2 is extremely fast and efficient, even when renaming
thousands of files at once.
Undo Functionality
: Any renaming operation can be easily undone to allow
the easy correction of mistakes.
Extensive Documentation
: F2 is well-documented with clear, practical
examples to help you make the most of its features without confusion.
⚡ Installation
If you're a Go developer, F2 can be installed with
go install
(requires v1.23
or later):
go install github.com/ayoisaiah/f2/v2/cmd/f2@latest
Other installation methods are
documented here
or check
out the
releases page
to download a
pre-compiled binary for your operating system.

data.article_summary: 该仓库包含一个名为 "Find And Replace" (far) 的命令行工具的代码，它可以快速、灵活地在文件和文件夹中搜索和替换文本。主要功能包括：搜索文本、快速替换文本、针对特定文件或目录操作、支持干运行（即将推出）以及智能大小写处理。工具灵感来源于Sublime Text的查找与替换功能。安装需通过git克隆并使用Cargo构建，支持指定文本和目标路径进行操作。该项目基于Apache-2.0许可证，欢迎提交改进建议和功能请求。

— a fast, flexible command-line tool to search and replace text across files and folders.
Features
🔍 Find text in files or folders

🧠 Smart casing support (e.g.

Bar
,
FOO
→
BAR
)
💡 Inspired by Sublime Text’s find & replace

git clone https://github.com/ibilalkayy/far.git
cd
far
cargo build --release

far --find

data.title: Live facial recognition cameras may become 'commonplace' as police use soars
data.author: c-oreills
data.article_summary:
英国《卫报》和Liberty Investigates的联合调查显示，英格兰和威尔士的警方正加速使用实时面部识别技术，2024年扫描了近470万张人脸，是2023年的两倍多。尽管该技术尚未被议会立法提及，警方却在大力部署，包括计划在伦敦和威尔士的交通枢纽安装固定摄像头。实时面部识别通过将监控摄像头捕捉到的人脸与警方的观察名单进行比对，而 retrospective facial recognition（ retrospective面部识别）则用于在数据库中进行匹配。

尽管有法院曾裁定南威尔士警方的使用是非法的，且该技术被指对黑人误识别率较高，警方仍在扩大使用范围。目前，英国政府正在考虑是否需要为这项技术制定专门的法律框架，但尚未提供具体细节。批评者认为警方在“自我监管”，且未经授权使用大量面部图像数据，如护照和移民数据库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公共安全监控技术（如摄像头、自动车牌识别等）的合法性、隐私影响以及对社会的影响。

不同观点：
• **[beloch]** 认为需要法律将监控摄像头视为类似于窃听装置的工具，数据只能通过特定范围的搜查令访问，用于合法调查而非日常监控和个人行为分析。例如，可以用于确定犯罪现场的人员，但不能用于长时间重建某人的日常生活网络。

• **[masfuerte]** 指出，类似的情况曾发生在自动车牌识别系统（ANPR）上。警方建立了全国范围的ANPR摄像头网络，事后信息专员认为可能非法，但建议修改法律使警方违法行为合法化，而非进行起诉。

• **[smcin]** 提到了美国亚特兰大的“警察城市”（Cop City）项目，尽管有反对声音，该项目仍顺利启动，并与多家公司和基金会有关联。同时，提到英国和威尔士的警察致命 shootings 较少，并提供了相关报告链接。

• **[caditinpiscinam]** 以讽刺的方式提出，如果继续增加监控，不如让人穿上带有QR码的衣服，直接公开个人信息，以节省处理时间。

• **[ceinewydd]** 描述了英国ANPR系统的发展历史及其广泛应用，包括平均速度监控和固定摄像头对违规行为的自动处罚，指出这种系统在英国比美国更为严格。

• **[darepublic]** 认为，尽管执法部门越来越依赖自动化监控，但对严重犯罪（如伪造车牌）的罚款和执法不力，导致对普通公众的严格惩罚和对顽固犯罪分子的放任。

• **[kwertyoowiyop]** 以幽默方式指出，监控技术的普及会让谋杀谜案剧更难写，因为难以解释为何没有关键区域的交通摄像头覆盖。

• **[Buttons840]** 希望那些掌握权力的人首先被曝光，表达了对权力滥用的担忧。

• **[octo888]** 认为广泛的监控不会减少犯罪，反而会对无辜人群产生寒蝉效应，推动更多权威主义，并为私人公司带来巨大利润。

• **[vladms]** 指出，这些系统并非因为小阴谋而出现，而是因为许多人认为它们可以接受且未组织起来反对。前警察认为自动化会使警察工作更安全、更容易。

• **[Oarch]** 质疑是否会禁止所有类型的面部遮盖物，尤其是在文化敏感的英国。

• **[electrondood]** 提到，执法人员可以穿便衣执行任务，而不展示身份证明或搜查令，暗示这种做法存在问题。

补充讨论：
- **隐私与合法性问题**：许多评论关注监控技术的隐私问题，以及如何在法律框架内使用这些数据。
- **执法效率与公平性**：有人担心监控对普通公众过于严格，但对顽固犯罪分子效果不佳。
- **社会影响与权力滥用**：评论提到了监控对社会的寒蝉效应，以及对权力滥用的担忧。
- **文化与法律差异**：讨论中涉及了英国和美国在法律和文化上的差异，以及这些差异如何影响监控技术的应用。

44082326.article_content:
Live facial recognition involves matching faces caught on cameras against a police watchlist in real time.
Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
Live facial recognition involves matching faces caught on cameras against a police watchlist in real time.
Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images
Facial recognition
Live facial recognition cameras may become ‘commonplace’ as police use soars
Exclusive: The Guardian and Liberty Investigates find police in England and Wales believe expansion is likely after 4.7m faces scanned in 2024
Valuable tool or cause for alarm? Facial ID quietly becoming part of police’s arsenal
Daniel Boffey
and
Mark Wilding
Sat 24 May 2025 12.41 EDT
First published on Sat 24 May 2025 12.00 EDT
Share
Police believe live facial recognition cameras may become “commonplace” in
England
and Wales, according to internal documents, with the number of faces scanned having doubled to nearly 5m in the last year.
A joint investigation by the Guardian and
Liberty Investigates
highlights the speed at which the technology is becoming a staple of British policing.
Major funding is being allocated and hardware bought, while the British state is also looking to enable police forces to more easily access the full spread of its image stores, including passport and immigration databases, for retrospective facial recognition searches.
Live facial recognition involves the matching of faces caught on surveillance camera footage against a police watchlist in real time, in what campaigners liken to the continual finger printing of members of the public as they go about their daily lives.
Retrospective facial recognition software is used by the police to match images on databases with those caught on CCTV and other systems.
According to one funding document drawn up by South
Wales
police as part of a proposal to put the West End of London or Cardiff rail station under live facial recognition cameras and released by the Metropolitan police under the Freedom of Information Act, it is believed “the use of this technology could become commonplace in our city centres and transport hubs around England and Wales”.
The first fixed live facial recognition cameras will be fitted for a trial in Croydon, south London, later this summer.
The expansion comes despite facial recognition failing to be referenced in any act of parliament.
Campaigners claim the police have been allowed to “self regulate” their use of the technology. Officers have in the past used a setting that was subsequently shown to disproportionately misidentify black people.
After a court of appeal judgment in 2020, which found that South Wales police’s
use of live facial recognition cameras
had been unlawful, the College of Policing provided guidance that “the threshold needs to be set with care to maximise the probability of returning true alerts while keeping the false alert rate to an acceptable level”.
There remains nothing in law to direct forces on the threshold or technology used.
The policing minister, Diane Johnson, told parliament earlier this month that she recognised “a need to consider whether a bespoke legislative framework governing the use of live facial recognition technology for law enforcement purposes is needed” but the Home Office is yet to provide details.
Facial recognition cameras were first
trialled in London
and south Wales from 2016 but the speed at which police forces are rolling out the technology has accelerated over the last 12 months.
The investigation by the Guardian and Liberty found:
Police forces scanned nearly 4.7m faces with live facial recognition cameras last year – more than twice as many as in 2023. Live facial recognition vans were deployed at least 256 times in 2024, according to official deployment records, up from 63 the year before.
A roving unit of 10 live facial recognition vans that can be sent anywhere in the country will be made available within days – increasing national capacity. Eight police forces have deployed the technology. The Met has four vans.
Police forces have considered fixed infrastructure creating a “zone of safety” by covering the West End of London with a network of live facial recognition cameras. Met officials said this remained a possibility.
Forces almost doubled the number of retrospective facial recognition searches made last year using the police national database (PND) from 138,720 in 2023 to 252,798. The PND contains custody mug shots, millions of which have been
found to be stored unlawfully
of people who have never been charged with or convicted of an offence.
More than 1,000 facial recognition searches using the UK passport database were carried out in the last two years, and officers are increasingly searching for matches on the Home Office immigration database, with requests up last year, to 110. Officials have concluded that using the passport database for facial recognition is “not high risk” and “is not controversial”, according to internal documents.

• **[beloch]** 认为需要法律将监控摄像头视为类似于窃听装置的工具，数据只能通过特定范围的搜查令访问，用于合法调查而非日常监控和个人行为分析。例如，可以用于确定犯罪现场的人员，但不能用于长时间重建某人的日常生活网络。

• **[masfuerte]** 指出，类似的情况曾发生在自动车牌识别系统（ANPR）上。警方建立了全国范围的ANPR摄像头网络，事后信息专员认为可能非法，但建议修改法律使警方违法行为合法化，而非进行起诉。

• **[smcin]** 提到了美国亚特兰大的“警察城市”（Cop City）项目，尽管有反对声音，该项目仍顺利启动，并与多家公司和基金会有关联。同时，提到英国和威尔士的警察致命 shootings 较少，并提供了相关报告链接。

• **[caditinpiscinam]** 以讽刺的方式提出，如果继续增加监控，不如让人穿上带有QR码的衣服，直接公开个人信息，以节省处理时间。

• **[ceinewydd]** 描述了英国ANPR系统的发展历史及其广泛应用，包括平均速度监控和固定摄像头对违规行为的自动处罚，指出这种系统在英国比美国更为严格。

• **[darepublic]** 认为，尽管执法部门越来越依赖自动化监控，但对严重犯罪（如伪造车牌）的罚款和执法不力，导致对普通公众的严格惩罚和对顽固犯罪分子的放任。

• **[kwertyoowiyop]** 以幽默方式指出，监控技术的普及会让谋杀谜案剧更难写，因为难以解释为何没有关键区域的交通摄像头覆盖。

• **[Buttons840]** 希望那些掌握权力的人首先被曝光，表达了对权力滥用的担忧。

• **[octo888]** 认为广泛的监控不会减少犯罪，反而会对无辜人群产生寒蝉效应，推动更多权威主义，并为私人公司带来巨大利润。

• **[vladms]** 指出，这些系统并非因为小阴谋而出现，而是因为许多人认为它们可以接受且未组织起来反对。前警察认为自动化会使警察工作更安全、更容易。

• **[Oarch]** 质疑是否会禁止所有类型的面部遮盖物，尤其是在文化敏感的英国。

• **[electrondood]** 提到，执法人员可以穿便衣执行任务，而不展示身份证明或搜查令，暗示这种做法存在问题。

补充讨论：
- **隐私与合法性问题**：许多评论关注监控技术的隐私问题，以及如何在法律框架内使用这些数据。
- **执法效率与公平性**：有人担心监控对普通公众过于严格，但对顽固犯罪分子效果不佳。
- **社会影响与权力滥用**：评论提到了监控对社会的寒蝉效应，以及对权力滥用的担忧。
- **文化与法律差异**：讨论中涉及了英国和美国在法律和文化上的差异，以及这些差异如何影响监控技术的应用。

data.title: It is time to stop teaching frequentism to non-statisticians (2012)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 文章主张停止向非统计学专业的学生教授频率统计学方法，转而教授贝叶斯方法。作者认为，这样做可以减少使用统计学时的困惑和对确定性的过度自信。频率统计学常导致误解和误用，而贝叶斯方法提供了一种更直观且符合逻辑的统计推断方式。作者建议在本科教育中进行这种转变，以提高学生的统计学理解和应用能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：贝叶斯统计与频率统计在科学教育和应用中的优劣及适用性

不同观点：
• **支持贝叶斯统计**：robwwilliams认为贝叶斯统计在高级统计中逐渐占优，但更重要的是应首先教本科生探索性数据分析。他推荐了Mosteller和Tukey的《数据分析与回归》以及Judea Pearl的《为什么》。他认为贝叶斯方法在结合先验信息上有优势。

• **频率统计的辩护**：perrygeo指出频率统计方法本身并没有错，只是在某些情况下被不合理地普遍应用。频率方法在处理真正的随机现象时是一个方便的数学捷径，但不应强制每个出版物都使用这些捷径。频率统计在科学再现性危机中的角色表明了问题。

• **实用主义立场**：usgroup认为统计学首先是应用数学，扩展以处理特定问题的不确定性。他们强调建模和在不确定性下为模型辩护的能力，而不是特定于贝叶斯或频率的方法。不同领域使用不同的工具处理不确定性，这些工具不应被对立起来。

• **对新方法的怀疑**：getnormality对改变当前方法持怀疑态度，认为当前方法的问题是已知的，而新方法的问题尚未充分了解或广为人知。

• **工具论**：nurettin认为贝叶斯和频率统计都是工具，而非意识形态。他举例说明在不同情况下不同工具的适用性，反对将这些工具对立起来。

补充讨论：
• **频率统计与贝叶斯统计的核心区别**：hnuser123456总结了两种方法在概率定义、参数处理、先验信息使用和推断对象上的区别，并提出通过详细描述实验条件可以增加结果的可信度。

• **非同行评审文章的讨论**：NewsaHackO质疑为何随机人员可以提交非同行评审的文章到预印本库，建议使用博客等其他平台。

• **实际例子和资源寻找**：throwaway81523回忆曾看到一篇关于频率统计优于贝叶斯方法的博客文章，但无法找到。chuckadams分享了一个有助于理解统计误区的xkcd漫画链接。

• **文章版本问题**：bmacho提到文章自2012年以来的一些技术性问题，如PDF被替换，但内容基本保持不变。

争议焦点：
• **贝叶斯统计与频率统计在教育和应用中的优先性**：支持贝叶斯统计的人认为应优先教授贝叶斯方法及其应用，而实用主义者和频率统计支持者则认为应根据具体问题选择合适的方法，而非局限于某一种方法。

• **工具的对立与实用**：一些评论者认为贝叶斯和频率统计应被视为互补的工具，而非互斥的意识形态。

data.title: You're a little company, now act like one
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论小公司在初期常犯的错误：试图通过专业化的营销语言和大公司形象来吸引客户，但实际上这往往适得其反。作者以自身经验为例，指出小公司不应模仿大企业的做法，而应专注于吸引早期采用者（Early Adopters）。这些早期客户乐于尝试不完善的新技术，并愿意与创始人直接交流和提供反馈。小公司应接受自身的不完美，明确目标客户群，特别是那些愿意承担风险、寻求竞争优势的早期用户。文章强调，小公司应展示真实自我，而不是假装成大企业，以此赢得适合自己的客户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小型创业公司应如何定位和展示自己

不同观点：
• **不假装成大公司，展现真实自我**：[neilv]认为小型创业公司不应该假装成大公司，而是应展现自己作为一个高度专注和技能出众的团队，直接与客户合作，确保项目的成功。他提到，过分注重表面工作（如制作精美的网站）反而削弱了公司的优势。相比之下，大公司的销售人员无法像小公司那样真正专注于单个客户的成功。

• **小型公司的优势在于灵活和直接沟通**：[eszed]指出，作为中型公司的客户，他更愿意与小型公司合作，因为可以直接与工程师沟通，从而帮助改进产品。虽然小型公司可能会经历成长、融资或收购后的变质，导致早期优势丧失，但这种直接沟通和合作仍然是小型公司的一大优势。

• **在某些行业需要看起来更大**：[myflash13]提到，在金融科技等需要信任的行业，小型公司可能需要显得更大，以获得客户信任。他分享了自己因为是 solo 创始人而失去客户的经历，表明在这些行业中，客户更倾向于信任大公司。

• **小型公司的独特卖点**：[landgenoot]认为小型公司应该利用其小而灵活的特点，不必追求大公司的做法。他举例说，一个小企业主通过WhatsApp运营业务，这提供了独特的客户体验，比数字化的客户门户更有效。

• **脆弱性作为超级力量**：[3dsnano]提出，脆弱性如果利用得当，可以带来更真实的对话，并筛选出那些不理解公司价值的客户。这与直接展现公司的真实状态相关，能够带来更深层次的客户关系。

• **简化与客户的互动，减少形式化**：[danenania]支持不假装成大公司，认为这样不仅更容易，还能带来更多的乐趣和真实的连接。他指出，保持真实不仅能减少与客户互动的痛苦，还能吸引到真正与公司价值观契合的人。

补充讨论：
• **历史讨论和相关文章**：[latchkey]和[jmkni]提到了之前的讨论和Paul Graham的文章《Do Things that Don't Scale》，强调了小型公司在早期应采取不规模化的方式，专注于真实的客户互动。

• **AI行业的不同早期采用者**：[w10-1]提到，AI行业的早期采用者可能与其他技术基础设施的早期采用者不同，他们更关注收益，而不太了解如何推动技术前进。

争议焦点：小型公司是否应假装成大公司以获得客户信任，特别是在金融等需要高度信任的行业中。一些人认为小型公司应利用其灵活和直接沟通的优势，而另一些人则认为在某些情况下需要显得更大以获得客户信任。

44081494.article_content:
Youâre a little company, now act like one
by Jason Cohen on August 31, 2009
You’re afraid that looking like being a small company means you’ll lose sales. It’s actually the opposite – you’re alienating your best customers.
source
I talk to a lot of companies that are still hunting for customer #1, or a few sales have been made but
the ball isn’t rolling yet
.
Most of them are making the same mistake:
Their public persona is exactly wrong.
I know, because
I made the same mistake!
But I learned my lesson, and I’d like to share it with you.
Nobody’s this happy about installing new software.
Even before I had a single customer, I “knew” it was important to look professional. My website would need to look and feel like a “real company.” I need culture-neutral language complementing culturally-diverse clip-art photos of frighteningly chipper co-workers huddled around a laptop, awash in the thrill of configuring a JDBC connection to SQL Server 2008.
It also means adopting typical “marketing-speak,” so my “About Us” page started with:
Smart Bear is the leading provider of enterprise version control data-mining tools. Companies world-wide use Smart Bear’s Code Historian software for risk-analysis, root-cause discovery, and software development decision-support.
“Leading provider?” “Data mining?” I’m not even
sure what that means
. But you have to give me credit for an impressive quantity of hyphens.
source
That’s what you’re
supposed
to do right? That’s what other companies do, so it
must
be right. Who am I to break with tradition? Surely my potential customers would immediately close the browser if they read:
Hi, I’m Jason and I built an inexpensive tool for visualizing what’s in your version control system. It’s useful for answering questions like “When was the last time we changed this file?” Check it out and tell me what sucks!
I mean, can you
just imagine
a person with “Software Engineer III” on their business card taking me seriously if I talked like a human being? What if someone gets
offended by the word “sucks?”
No no, big companies want to see professional language!
But I was wrong.
I’ll explain why from the point of view of selling software over the web, but the same lesson applies to every little company trying to get off the ground.
Now repeat after me:
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
I’m telling you this having sold software to every size of company from indie hacker to IBM, and, well, to Lockheed Martin.
Your vision is to land $100k deals with big companiesâand you will! But not today. Today your product is a shaky version one-dot-oh with bugs you haven’t uncovered yet,
missing 90% of the features
big companies require, and with no significant documentation like case studies or a proper manual or
an ROI model
or a large, reference-able customer.
Today, you’re a complete mismatch with Lockheed Martin!
But there’s a nice big niche that’s a
perfect
match: Early Adopters.
Early Adopters
are people who
want
to live on the bleeding edge. They like new technology, even if buggy. They like working with teeny companies where they
have a personal relationship with the founders
, where they are showered with attention, and where their ideas are implemented before their very eyes. They don’t mind putting up with a hundred bugs so long as they get fixed fast. They want to be involved in the process.
The reason they’re willing to do that, is Early Adopters see new technology as a way for them to beat their competitors. They’re willing to take the risk, if it pays off in features that only they have, or distribution channels they can win in, or some other significant competitive advantage.
Most companies aren’t willing to take risks
for
any
reason, so this is a winning strategy for those willing to take risks.
Tom
is an Early Adopter. At Smart Bear I must have had ten or twenty of these folks before our product was stable enough and feature-rich enough to start getting attention from bigger companies.
The best part is, this is exactly the moment in your company’s life when you
need
Early Adopters to help you build the right product! You don’t need people who download, get discouraged, and then never call you back. You need a chatty Cathy who wants to dive in and help out.
In short, you need to
tightly define your ICP
, because those are the people who love you, for who you are, today, and therefore where you will be successful.
So now back to your website, your blog, your Twittersâyour public corporate persona generally.
What do you put up on your website that screams out to those potential Early Adopter Cheerleaders that you are exactly what they’re looking for

44081494.article_summary: 文章主要讨论小公司在初期常犯的错误：试图通过专业化的营销语言和大公司形象来吸引客户，但实际上这往往适得其反。作者以自身经验为例，指出小公司不应模仿大企业的做法，而应专注于吸引早期采用者（Early Adopters）。这些早期客户乐于尝试不完善的新技术，并愿意与创始人直接交流和提供反馈。小公司应接受自身的不完美，明确目标客户群，特别是那些愿意承担风险、寻求竞争优势的早期用户。文章强调，小公司应展示真实自我，而不是假装成大企业，以此赢得适合自己的客户。
44081494.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小型创业公司应如何定位和展示自己

不同观点：
• **不假装成大公司，展现真实自我**：[neilv]认为小型创业公司不应该假装成大公司，而是应展现自己作为一个高度专注和技能出众的团队，直接与客户合作，确保项目的成功。他提到，过分注重表面工作（如制作精美的网站）反而削弱了公司的优势。相比之下，大公司的销售人员无法像小公司那样真正专注于单个客户的成功。

• **小型公司的优势在于灵活和直接沟通**：[eszed]指出，作为中型公司的客户，他更愿意与小型公司合作，因为可以直接与工程师沟通，从而帮助改进产品。虽然小型公司可能会经历成长、融资或收购后的变质，导致早期优势丧失，但这种直接沟通和合作仍然是小型公司的一大优势。

• **在某些行业需要看起来更大**：[myflash13]提到，在金融科技等需要信任的行业，小型公司可能需要显得更大，以获得客户信任。他分享了自己因为是 solo 创始人而失去客户的经历，表明在这些行业中，客户更倾向于信任大公司。

• **小型公司的独特卖点**：[landgenoot]认为小型公司应该利用其小而灵活的特点，不必追求大公司的做法。他举例说，一个小企业主通过WhatsApp运营业务，这提供了独特的客户体验，比数字化的客户门户更有效。

• **脆弱性作为超级力量**：[3dsnano]提出，脆弱性如果利用得当，可以带来更真实的对话，并筛选出那些不理解公司价值的客户。这与直接展现公司的真实状态相关，能够带来更深层次的客户关系。

• **简化与客户的互动，减少形式化**：[danenania]支持不假装成大公司，认为这样不仅更容易，还能带来更多的乐趣和真实的连接。他指出，保持真实不仅能减少与客户互动的痛苦，还能吸引到真正与公司价值观契合的人。

补充讨论：
• **历史讨论和相关文章**：[latchkey]和[jmkni]提到了之前的讨论和Paul Graham的文章《Do Things that Don't Scale》，强调了小型公司在早期应采取不规模化的方式，专注于真实的客户互动。

• **AI行业的不同早期采用者**：[w10-1]提到，AI行业的早期采用者可能与其他技术基础设施的早期采用者不同，他们更关注收益，而不太了解如何推动技术前进。

争议焦点：小型公司是否应假装成大公司以获得客户信任，特别是在金融等需要高度信任的行业中。一些人认为小型公司应利用其灵活和直接沟通的优势，而另一些人则认为在某些情况下需要显得更大以获得客户信任。

data.title: DIY Cybersickness Remedies
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一些简单的技巧，可以帮助减少虚拟现实（VR）中可能引发晕动症的感知差异。作者马修·科克森（Matthew Coxon）是英国约克圣约翰大学的高级心理学讲师，他提出了三种具体方法来缓解VR引发的恶心感。这些技巧旨在通过调整视觉与身体感觉之间的冲突，提升用户在VR环境中的体验，从而更舒适地享受虚拟现实技术。文章强调，通过自我调整，用户可以有效应对VR带来的不适。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VR使用中的运动病问题及其相关因素

不同观点：
• **ranger207** 认为，VR运动 sickness 问题在使用几十小时后会逐渐消失。对于新的体验，可能需要再花一小时左右适应。他指出，如果为已有VR使用经验的用户设计内容，可以假设大多数用户已经适应了VR环境。
• **mattlondon** 对当前VR的使用情况表示怀疑，质疑是否还有人使用VR，尤其是用于游戏，或者认为VR头戴设备可能已经被闲置。他提出了VR是否只被少数人用来替代显示器的问题，并暗示这些场景不会导致运动病。
• **neilv** 提出三个问题：1) 为什么会有人愿意忍受VR带来的运动病？2) 对于容易晕动症或有前庭损伤的人，适应VR的技巧可能有帮助，即使他们并不觉得VR游戏有趣。3) 过度适应VR是否可能损害前庭系统，导致在现实中面对突然失衡时恢复能力下降？
• **paulryanrogers** 分享了个人经验，提到有冰滑经验的人可能更容易适应VR，因为滑冰和VR都有不自然的运动体验。他还提到虽然自己通过 persistence 适应了滑雪，但并未帮助他解决VR sickness。

补充讨论：
• **pavel_lishin** 以幽默的方式提到，他原以为文章会和《Johnny Mnemonic》相关，暗示对文章标题或主题的期望不同。

争议焦点：
• 关于VR运动病是否可以通过适应来解决存在不同看法。**ranger207** 认为适应是可行的，**neilv** 则担心过度适应可能导致其他健康问题。**mattlondon** 则对VR的普及性和实用性提出了质疑。

总结：讨论主要围绕VR运动病的适应性、使用场景的广泛性以及潜在健康风险展开，不同用户基于个人经验和观察提出了各自的见解。

data.title: The Decline of Usability: Revisited (2023)
data.author: turrini
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了用户界面设计中的可用性问题，特别是自三年前作者首次发表相关评论以来的情况。作者重申，当前的用户界面设计在可用性方面没有改善，且相关讨论中反复出现无效的辩论，如对过去界面的否定或对“进步”的盲目推崇。作者强调，可用性是指系统让用户高效、安全、满意地完成任务的能力，而不仅仅是界面的美观或功能的增加。文章还讨论了界面设计中的一致性问题，特别是在Windows 8之前各大厂商普遍遵循的基本操作原则。作者指出，虽然界面 redesign 有时能提升可用性，但应基于实际研究和数据，而非主观臆断。最后，作者呼吁关注如“可供性”等久经研究的设计概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：现代用户界面（UI）设计的复杂性、可用性及其对用户体验的影响

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如hipinspire）批评现代UI设计过度简化，将复杂操作（如购买昂贵商品）与简单任务混为一谈，导致用户体验不佳。
• puttycat表示现代应用程序（如Spotify）的UI变得过于复杂，使得基本操作变得困难，甚至让有经验的用户也感到困惑。
• mcswell指出许多现代UI控件位置分散，例如Visual Studio Code中的控件放置不直观，增加了使用难度。
• padjo提到滚动条等基本UI元素的消失是出于美学考虑，但牺牲了功能性，导致用户在使用时遇到困难。
• bigbuppo批评“汉堡菜单”设计不直观，即使是经验丰富的技术人员也常常不知道如何操作，主张在功能性和美学之间找到平衡。

补充讨论：
• zzo38computer认为现代UI库和编程环境的缺陷也是导致不良UI设计的原因之一，并强调了键盘快捷键和文档的重要性。
• mystified5016指出现代集成开发环境（IDE）过度简化，去除了复杂功能，导致专业程序员在处理复杂任务时效率低下。
• skydhash建议UI设计应根据具体领域（如文字处理或3D建模）进行调整，而不是一味追求公司品牌和过度简化，并推荐使用Emacs、TUI和CLI工具来避免现代UI的困扰。
• Animats讨论了Blender和GIMP等软件中状态复杂性和菜单设计的问题，强调了用户在操作时难以判断当前状态的困难。
• 有人提出历史上Mac或Lisa可能比IBM Common User Access更早引入 ellipsis ("...") 菜单设计，讨论了UI设计的历史渊源。
• awinter-py和jll29分别对一些图标设计（如“存档”图标）和简化菜单（如“+”或“...”）表示困惑和不满。
• mvdtnz和jll29对滚动条自动隐藏和开关设计表示不解，认为这些设计增加了不必要的复杂性。
• foxglacier分享了关于开关设计的个人经历，指出即使是硬件开关设计也存在不一致和混乱。

争议焦点：
• 现代UI设计是否应优先考虑功能性而非美学，特别是在处理复杂任务的应用程序中。
• 汉堡菜单和其他简化设计的直观性及其对用户体验的影响。
• 滚动条等基本UI元素的隐藏是否合理，以及其对用户操作的影响。

{ datagubbe }
datagubbe.se
»
the decline of usability: revisited
The Decline of Usability: Revisited
In which we once more delve into the world of user interface design.
Autumn 2023
Three years ago, I wrote
a rant about the problems
of our current UI paradigm. The complaints I voiced were hardly new or unique, neither was the text what I'd consider my best writing. It was, honestly, mostly a way to blow off steam. It seems I struck a nerve, though, because it's proven to be one of the most popular texts I've published here. For some time, I've thought about writing a follow-up, and a recent resurgence in the text's popularity prompted me to finally do so.
I didn't (and still don't) have any delusions that my ramblings will somehow affect anything. And, in three years' time, nothing has indeed changed - at least not for the better. The most depressing part is perhaps that the debate around these issues hasn't changed one iota, either. The same non-arguments crop up all the time when discussing these issues:
"Well, gramps, maybe things weren't super duper great in the past, either?" "Where's the research, dude?" "It's progress, man. Progress! You can't stop progress!" "Uhhhhm, actually, compadre, we can do so much stuff with computers nowadays! That's usability, broseph!"
If I sound salty, it's because I am. Deal with it.
What were we talking about?
Usability, as defined by Wikipedia, is "the capacity of a system to provide a condition for its users to perform the tasks safely, effectively, and efficiently while enjoying the experience." Its relation to software is further specified: "In software engineering, usability is the degree to which a software can be used by specified consumers to achieve quantified objectives with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction in a quantified context of use."
Let's go on with Wikipedia:
"The primary notion of usability is that an object designed with a generalized users' psychology and physiology in mind is, for example:
More efficient to use — takes less time to accomplish a particular task.
Easier to learn — operation can be learned by observing the object.
More satisfying to use."
In short,
usability is the ease with which a predetermined task can be accomplished.
Consequently, "It looks fresh" isn't usability; it's aesthetics. Likewise, the lack of a specific program feature isn't the same as being able to use it as easily, efficiently and safely as possible. Looking for the power switch on a hand-cranked drill is silly, but maybe we should complain if we had to operate power tools with our pinky fingers. Similarly, a word processor without a mail merge function is perhaps intended for other types of word processing - such as writing novels. Hence,
being usable in many different situations
isn't automatically the same as
having a high level of usability
.
Conceptual consistency
In my original text, some arguments deal with static GUI design (such as low contrast or excessive use of screen real estate), but many do not. Some are about consistency: consistency over time, consistency across applications and consistency across platforms.
Pure, static GUI design is a
subset
of usability: poor design choices, such as low contrast and illegible fonts, will lead to worse usability. It is, however, not always clear where to draw the line between what we call GUI (toolkit) design, UI design, usability and UX. One affects the other, roughly in the order listed, from the ground up.
All three forms of consistency (across time, application and platform) were, until roughly the release of Windows 8, honoured by most major vendors. When I talk about consistency, it's not to be understood as the exact same look, widget for widget and icon for icon -  it means adhering to basic standard principles of operation.
One
such example are the "File, Edit, View, Help" dropdown menus, recognizable between different operating systems, programs and UI toolkits. Sure, Java Swing looked a bit different than Win32, but they were still based around the same basic notions and concepts as all the other toolkits on the market.
This is not to say that consistency always trumps everything else: sometimes, real improvement of usability
can
be obtained through a complete interface overhaul. Windows 95 is a good example of that.
Show us the research, dude!
In discussions like these, there's usually at least one person who shows up to demand data or research, but curiously never presents anything to back up their own claims about modern UI superiority. But, by all means. The concepts I champion have been around for decades. Many of them have been studied in detail, some of them even build on ideas as old as - or older than - computers themselves.
One such concept is that of
affordances
, meaning how the look and shape of certain objects communicate information about how the object can be operated. A push button that protrudes from the surrounding surface, for example. Some affordances come more or less nat

data.title: Peer Programming with LLMs, for Senior+ Engineers
data.author: pmbanugo
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了高级工程师如何通过与大型语言模型（LLM）进行同伴编程来提升工作效率。尽管LLM在编码和调试方面有帮助，但也存在浪费时间的情况。文章汇集了几位高级工程师的博客帖子，分享了他们使用LLM的实际经验和技巧，包括：

1. **实用AI技术**：Sean Goedecke介绍了两种主要方法——"第二意见"技术和"一次性调试脚本"技术。

May 24, 2025
Peer Programming with LLMs, For Senior+ Engineers
Programming with LLMs is both promising and frustrating. While these AI assistants can help with coding and debugging, they often waste time too. Yet for senior engineers,
pair
peer programming with LLMs shows real potential.
This article is a collection of blog posts written by other senior or staff+ engineers exploring the use of LLM in their work, without the usual hype or buzzwords from the usual suspects. I hope you find them useful and inspiring.
Articles and Resources
Practical AI techniques for daily engineering work
by Sean Goedecke
: Sean shares two major ways he uses AI in his daily work â
The âSecond opinionâ technique
and
The âThrowaway debugging scriptsâ technique
. Iâve been using the âsecond opinionâ technique in recent weeks, so it resonated with me. Given the right context/problem, Iâd like to try the âthrowaway debugging scriptsâ technique as well. Sean also shares some other tips that can help you get started with using LLM tools for your work.
Harper Reedâs LLM Codegen Workflow
: Harper shares his workflow for using LLMs for code generation. Hereâs a summary of how he uses it:
Brainstorm spec, then co-plan a plan, then execute using LLM codegen.
REPEAT
.
I like the idea of using LLMs to brainstorm and co-plan before executing it. Iâve not been successful using this technique to build a complete feature or prototype. Maybe Iâm doing it slightly differently, and it ends up being a lot of hours chatting with an LLM. However, Iâm grateful for the times it helps me quit a project early, given that I realize itâs going to require more time and resources than I imagined. Dig into the blog post and steal this technique for your next feature or weekend project.
Documenting Your Prompts a Best Practice for Success
by Lee Boonstra
: This is a short and concise post about the importance of documenting your prompts when using LLMs. Itâs the only post Iâve seen about documenting your prompts, and I think itâs a great idea. I think itâs a great idea because Iâm exploring ways to use LLM tools for various kinds of work, and I found myself saving prompts with the goal of reviewing the ones that worked best. My approach isnât structured and this post gave me a few ideas on how to do it better.
ChatGPT is dumber than it looks
by Seth Godin:
This is a short and
somewhat
philosophical post that reminds us that LLMs are not as smart as many think they are. Although he sings the praise for Claude, I think the approach he described is useful for any LLM. He suggest that you should â
figure out how to create patterns and processes where you can use it as the useful tool itâs becoming
â.
Thatâs A Wrap
There you go, a small collection of resources I found useful and think can help you explore the use of LLMs in your work. If you have any other resources or articles that you think should be included in this list or that I should read, please let me know using any of my social handles at the end of the article.
Iâll finish with an
excerpt from Sethâs blog
â
When you get stuck, first ask Claude, then ask a human.
What do you think?

主要讨论点：Boggle问题解决的成就、技术实现、计算资源使用及其背后的算法问题。

不同观点：
• [smcin] 强调了Vanderkam自2004年以来独自研究Boggle问题的努力和过程，包括利用Google的硬件资源，并通过博客记录。
• [sireat] 认为Vanderkam的成就是算法课程中Branch and Bound方法的一个有趣应用例子，并询问了具体的上、下界估计方法。
• [robinhouston] 对这一技术故事被主流媒体报道感到惊讶，并好奇金融时报的记者是如何发现这个故事的。
• [cgreerrun] 赞赏了使用C++和Python结合的编程方式，认为这种组合在性能和开发速度之间取得了良好平衡。
• [throwaway81523] 对比了Google Cloud服务器和Hetzner上的Ryzen 5950X服务器在计算时间和成本上的差异，指出Google Cloud的服务器可能频率较低，实际计算时间可能相当于在其他硬件上的一到两个月。
• [jebarker] 认为虽然Boggle问题看似不重要，但Vanderkam的坚持令人钦佩，并将其与发现新梅森素数的成就相比较。
• [sphars] 对Vanderkam在大量可能组合中大幅削减计算量表示钦佩，指出其计算过程的高效性。
• [lowbloodsugar] 对Boggle问题中可能组合数量的计算提出异议，认为应该是6^16而非26^16。
• [everyone] 讨论了在Scrabble和Boggle游戏中，单纯追求分数与追求有意义的词汇之间的张力。

data.title: Tachy0n: The Last 0day Jailbreak
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者Siguza在2020年发现并利用的一个iOS内核漏洞（tachy0n），该漏洞影响了iOS 13.0至13.5，并在unc0ver v5.0.0中发布。这是当时一个罕见的0day漏洞，因为苹果在一周后为此专门发布了补丁。作者解释了这个漏洞的发现过程，以及它如何通过回归测试被重新找到。漏洞存在于lio_listio系统调用中，涉及一个竞态条件，导致内核内存重复释放，从而可以被利用进行内核权限提升。这个漏洞的特殊之处在于它曾被当作1day使用过，但由于苹果的疏忽，它未被完全修复，最终成为0day。作者还回顾了类似漏洞的历史，如SockPuppet，强调了苹果在回归测试方面的不足。

44083388.article_content:
Siguza, 23. May 2025
tachy0n
The last 0day jailbreak.
0. Introduction
Hey.
Long time no see, huh?
People have speculated over the years that someone “bought my silence”, or asked me whether I had moved my blog posts to some other place, but no. Life just got in the way.
This is not the blog post with which I planned to return, but it’s the one for which all the research is said and done, so that’s what you’re getting. I have plenty more that I wanna do, but I’ll be happy if I can even manage to put out two a year.
Now,
tachy0n
. This is an old exploit, for iOS 13.0 through 13.5, released in
unc0ver
v5.0.0 on May 23rd, 2020, exactly 5 years ago today. It was a fairly standard kernel LPE for the time, but one thing that made it noteworthy is that it was dropped as an 0day, affecting the latest iOS version at the time, leading Apple to
release a patch
for just this bug a week later. This is something that used to be common a decade ago, but has become extremely rare - so rare, in fact, that is has never happened again after this.
Another thing that made it noteworthy is that, despite having been an 0day on iOS 13.5, it had actually been exploited before - by me and friends - but as a 1day at the time. And that is where this whole story starts.
In early 2020,
Pwn20wnd
(a jailbreak author, not to be confused with Pwn2Own, the event) contacted me, saying he had found an 0day reachable from the app sandbox, and was asking whether I’d be willing to write an exploit for it. At the time I had been working on
checkra1n
for a couple of months, so I figured going back to kernel research was a welcome change of scenery, and I agreed. But where did this bug come from? It was extremely unlikely that someone would’ve just sent him this bug for free, with no strings attached. And despite being a jailbreak author, he wasn’t doing security research himself, so it was equally unlikely that he would discover such a bug. And yet, he did.
The way he managed to beat a trillion dollar corporation was through the kind of simple but tedious and boring work that Apple sucks at: regression testing.
Because, you see: this has happened before. On iOS 12,
SockPuppet
was one of the big exploits used by jailbreaks. It was found and reported to Apple by
Ned Williamson
from Project Zero, patched by Apple in iOS 12.3, and subsequently unrestricted on the Project Zero bug tracker. But against all odds, it then resurfaced on iOS 12.4, as if it had never been patched. I can only speculate that this was because Apple likely forked XNU to a separate branch for that version and had failed to apply the patch there, but this made it evident that they had no regression tests for this kind of stuff. A gap that was both easy and potentially very rewarding to fill. And indeed, after implementing regression tests for just a few known 1days, Pwn got a hit.
So just for a moment, forget everything you know about kheap separation, forget all the task port mitigations, forget SSV and SPTM… and let’s look at some stuff from the good old times.
1. Lightspeed
First, a quick recap on this bug. This is the
Lightspeed
bug from Synacktiv (CVE-2020-9859 and possibly CVE-2018-4344). It’s in the
lio_listio
syscall, which lets you do asynchronous and/or batched file I/O. To keep track of all submitted I/O ops, the kernel allocates this struct:
struct
aio_lio_context
{
int
io_waiter
;
int
io_issued
;
int
io_completed
;
};
The actual work is then performed on a separate thread, which is also responsible for freeing this struct once all I/O has been completed (in
do_aio_completion
):
/* Are we done with this lio context? */
if
(
lio_context
->
io_issued
==
lio_context
->
io_completed
)
{
lastLioCompleted
=
TRUE
;
}
/*
* free the LIO context if the last lio completed and no thread is
* waiting
*/
if
(
lastLioCompleted
&&
(
waiter
==
0
))
{
free_lio_context
(
lio_context
);
}
But in the case where
nothing
has been scheduled at all, that code path will never be hit, and so the
current
thread has to free this struct again, right from
lio_listio
:
case
LIO_NOWAIT
:
/* If no IOs were issued must free it (rdar://problem/45717887) */
if
(
lio_context
->
io_issued
==
0
)
{
free_context
=
TRUE
;
}
break
;
if
(
free_context
)
{
free_lio_context
(
lio_context
);
}
The problem is just that this check is racy. If work
has
been submitted to the other thread, but it has
already completed
by the time this check runs, then
lio_context
is a dangling pointer here. You can check the
original blog post
for more details, but in order to exploit this, we want the following sequence of events:
lio_listio
allocates
lio_context
.
The work completes and
do_aio_completion
frees
lio_context
.
We reallocate the freed memory with something we control, such that
lio_context->io_issued == 0
.
lio_listio
sees
lio_context->io_issued == 0
and frees our allocated object.
We reallocate it again with something else, and now have two entirely different allocations pointing to the same memory.
Now, we’re targeting 64
44083388.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者Siguza在2020年发现并利用的一个iOS内核漏洞（tachy0n），该漏洞影响了iOS 13.0至13.5，并在unc0ver v5.0.0中发布。这是当时一个罕见的0day漏洞，因为苹果在一周后为此专门发布了补丁。作者解释了这个漏洞的发现过程，以及它如何通过回归测试被重新找到。漏洞存在于lio_listio系统调用中，涉及一个竞态条件，导致内核内存重复释放，从而可以被利用进行内核权限提升。这个漏洞的特殊之处在于它曾被当作1day使用过，但由于苹果的疏忽，它未被完全修复，最终成为0day。作者还回顾了类似漏洞的历史，如SockPuppet，强调了苹果在回归测试方面的不足。

data.title: Please Fund More Science (2020)
data.author: ssuds
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了结束新冠疫情、恢复正常生活的三种可能途径：开发出有效疫苗使病毒基本停止传播，找到有效治疗方法使人们不再恐惧，或建立完善的检测、追踪、戴口罩和隔离文化。作者认为，目前政府对研发的资助不足，私营部门和慈善机构虽能部分填补空缺，但并非长久之计。然而，生物科技公司和研究实验室正以惊人速度专注于解决这一问题，展现出空前的创新精神。作者呼吁投资者和捐赠者将更多资源投入科学研究，以应对当前及未来的疫情。这不仅有助于解决问题，还能带来新的机遇和乐观情绪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技精英与科学基金资助、新冠疫情的应对方式、私人和公共科研资助的比较与重要性

不同观点：
• Havoc认为科技精英正在资助的机构正在削减国家科学基金会（NSF）的资金，这具有讽刺意味。他引用了《纽约时报》的一篇文章来支持自己的观点，指出NSF正面临资金被大幅削减的困境。

• Yegg提供了十一个理由来支持科学资助的必要性，包括延长寿命、国防安全、经济回报、创新驱动、环境需求等。他认为这些理由足以说明科学资助的重要性，尤其是在多方面的回报上。

• WorkerBee28474认为新冠疫情并没有通过疫苗、治疗或测试追踪等方式结束，而是因为人们不再关心疫情而结束。这种观点强调了社会对疫情态度的转变，而非科学解决方案的实现。

• Petermcneeley支持WorkerBee28474的观点，并引用比尔·盖茨的文章，指出疫情实际上是通过第四种方式解决的，即变得像季节性流感一样。

• Jun8提出少数富人可以通过早期发掘人才、资助暑期学校、建立研究中心、设立大奖等方式对科学发展产生巨大影响。他详细描述了具体措施，并认为这些措施的成本相对较低，但效果显著。

• Babuloseo分享了自己利用加密货币挖矿剩余的GPU参与Folding@Home项目的经历，认为这种做法有助于科学研究，虽然个人贡献有限。

• EricDeb认为私人资助可能建立更好的激励机制，但公共研究的减少仍然令人遗憾，显示出对公共资助科研的重视。

• Toddm用Frank Zappa的名言讽刺硅谷文化，希望像Altman这样的人只是历史中的注脚，而不是像Frank Zappa那样成为永恒的头条。

• Light_hue_1认为这些超级富豪实际上并没有为科学提供多少资助，Altman和OpenAI、Google、微软等公司在这方面的贡献微乎其微，尽管这些公司有能力增加基础科学资助。

• PaulKeeble强调仍需开发能阻止新冠传播和治疗长新冠的疫苗，指出随着时间的推移，情况变得越来越严重，而政治决策导致资金大幅减少，呼吁更多关注和投入。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于科技精英和超级富豪是否应该且实际对科学资助的贡献大小，以及公共和私人资助在科研中的角色和重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及了应对新冠疫情的不同方式，特别是社会态度转变与科学解决方案的对比。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是如何通过早期发掘和培养人才、设立激励机制等方式有效推动科学进步，以及这些措施的可行性和成本效益。

44082968.article_content:
Experts on the COVID-19 pandemic seem to think there are three ways out—that is, for life, health, and the economy to return roughly to normal.
Either we get a vaccine good enough that R0 for the world goes below 1, a good enough treatment that people no longer need to be afraid, or we develop a great culture of testing, contract tracing, masks, and isolation.
I wish that the federal government were doing much more—it would be great to see even a few percent of the recent stimulus bill go to funding R+D.  But they don’t seem to be funding enough science, and although I think concerns about the private sector and philanthropy doing what the government is supposed to be doing are somewhat valid, there isn’t a great alternative right now.
On the positive side, I have never seen a field focused on one problem with such ferocity before.  The response of biotech companies and research labs is amazing, and the speed they are operating at seems to have increased by more than 10x.  It’s the best of the spirit of innovation, and it’s inspiring to see what these companies and research labs are doing.
Scientists can get us out of this.  What they need are money and connections.
Investors and donors—this is where we can help.  Please consider shifting some of your focus and capital to scientific efforts addressing the pandemic.  (And future pandemics too—I think this will be a before-and-after moment in the world, and until we can defend against new viruses quickly, things are going to be different.)
The learning curve is quick, and there are a lot of experts willing to help you with diligence.  It feels good to do something that might be useful, it’s interesting to do something totally new, and it will make you more optimistic.
If you make it known to your network that you want to fund efforts working on COVID-19, you’ll get flooded with opportunities.  And it’s always good to invest where the best founders are congregating.

data.title: Reinvent the Wheel
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了“不要重复造轮子”这句常见建议的局限性，认为鼓励探索和好奇心更为重要。文章指出，通过亲手实现和创造可以加深对技术的理解，即使最终不使用自己的成果，过程中也能学到很多。作者以轮子为例，说明重新发明可以带来更好的解决方案、帮助学习、解决问题以及激发创新。文章最后建议，为了获得洞见可以重新造轮子，而在追求实际影响时则应重用现有成果。作者还推荐了CodeCrafters平台以提升编程技能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该重新发明轮子（reinvent the wheel）

不同观点：
• **支持重新发明轮子**：
   - **学习与理解**：重新发明轮子是深入理解技术概念的有效方法，尤其是从基础原理开始构建能够增强对技术的掌握（[megadragon9], [gfalcao], [richardjennings]）。
   - **创新与创造**：重新发明轮子可以带来新的视角和创新，甚至可能创造出比现有技术更好的解决方案（[boricj], [gfalcao] 的引用）。
   - **避免不必要的依赖**：通过重新发明轮子，可以避免引入过多的外部依赖，从而简化系统（[begueradj]）。

• **反对盲目重新发明轮子**：
   - **时间和资源限制**：在工作环境或创业公司中，重新发明轮子可能会浪费宝贵的时间和资源，尤其是在有现成且成熟的解决方案时（[mullingitover], [dustingetz], [kayodelycaon]）。
   - **生产环境中的风险**：除非重新发明的轮子在质量和功能上能超越现有方案，否则在生产环境中使用可能带来风险（[wcfrobert], [kayodelycaon]）。

• **中立或条件支持**：
   - **时机和目的**：重新发明轮子应根据具体情况决定，特别是在学习或需要定制解决方案时是有意义的，但在商业项目中需谨慎（[wcfrobert], [richardjennings]）。
   - **理性决策**：团队应合理评估是否需要重新发明某些组件，避免陷入“非我发明”（Not Invented Here）综合症，但同时也应考虑市场现有方案的兼容性和成本（[awinter-py]）。

补充讨论：
• **哲学与社会批判**：有评论提到现代社会对冗余的过度排斥可能限制了个人创造力和多样性（[ppqqrr]）。
• **学习前人的工作**：在重新发明轮子之前，应先了解已有的工作，以避免重复劳动并从中获得启发（[cryptonector]）。
• **具体案例**：一些评论者分享了个人经验，如构建自定义机器学习库，展示了重新发明轮子的实际学习效果（[megadragon9]）。

争议焦点：重新发明轮子在学习和创新中的价值与其在实际项目中可能带来的时间和资源消耗之间的平衡。

44083467.article_content:
Published on 24th of May, 2025
Reinvent the Wheel
Tagged with
dev
culture
One of the most harmful pieces of advice is to not reinvent the wheel.
It usually comes from a good place, but is typically given by two groups of people:
those who tried to invent a wheel themselves and know how hard it is
those who never tried to invent a wheel and blindly follow the advice
Either way, both positions lead to a climate where curiosity and exploration gets discouraged. I’m glad that some people didn’t follow that advice; we owe them many of the conveniences of modern life.
Even on a surface level, the advice is bad: We have much better wheels today than 4500–3300 BCE when the first wheel was invented. It was also
crucially
important that wheels got reinvented throughout civilizations and cultures.
Note:
When I say “wheel” throughout this post, please replace it with whatever tool, protocol, service, technology, or other invention you’re personally interested in.
Inventing Wheels Is Learning
“What I cannot create, I do not understand”
–
Richard Feynman
, Physicist and Nobel Prize Winner
To
really
understand something on a fundamental level, you have to be able to implement a toy version first. It doesn’t matter if it’s any good; you can throw it away later.
In Computer Science, for example, there are many concepts that are commonly assumed to be beyond the abilities of mere mortals: protocols, cryptography, and web servers come to mind.
More people should know how these things work. And therefore I think people should not be afraid to recreate them.
Everything Is A Rabbit Hole
Too often, fundamental things are taken for granted. For example strings or paths are super complicated concepts in programming. It’s a great exercise to implement a string or a path library yourself if you’re interested in how they work.
Even if nobody ends up using your work, I bet you’ll learn a lot. For example:
There is an infinite complexity in everyday things.
Building something that even a single other person finds useful is a humbling experience.
Humans like you created these abstractions. They are not perfect and you can make different tradeoffs in your own design.
On the last point, everything is a tradeoff and there are dozens, sometimes hundreds of footguns with every toy problem.
Along the way, you will have to make decisions about correctness, simplicity, functionality, scalability, performance, resource usage, portability, and so on.
Your solution can be great in some of these things, but not all of them and not for all users. That also implies that existing solutions have flaws and might not be designed to solve your particular problem; no matter how well-established the solution is.
Going down rabbit holes is fun in its own way, but there is one other benefit: It is one of the few ways to level up as an engineer… but only if you don’t give up before you end up with a working version of what you tried to explore. If you jump between projects too often, you will learn nothing.
Reasons for Reinventing the Wheel
There are great reasons to reinvent the wheel:
Build a better wheel (for some definition of better)
Learn how wheels are made
Teach others about wheels
Learn about the inventors of wheels
Be able to change wheels or fix them when they break
Learn the tools needed to make wheels along the way
Learn a tiny slice of what it means to build a larger system (such as a vehicle)
Help someone in need of a very special wheel. Maybe for a wheelchair?
Who knows? The wheel you come up with might not be the best use for a car, but maybe for a… skateboard or a bike? Or you fail building a nicer wheel, but you come up with a better way to test wheels along the way. Heck, your wheel might not even be meant for transportation at all! It might be a potter’s wheel, “a machine used in the shaping (known as throwing) of clay into round ceramic ware”
according to Wikipedia
. You might end up building a totally different kind of wheel like a steering wheel or a flywheel. We need more people who think outside the box.
Reuse vs Reinvent
Of course, don’t disregard the works of others – study their work and reuse where you see fit. Don’t reinvent the wheel out of distrust or ignorance of the work of others. On the other side, if you never tried to put your knowledge to the test, how would you ever learn enough about your field to advance it?
I observed you can move very quickly by running little experiments. Especially in software engineering, building small prototypes is cheap and quick. Solve your own problem, start small, keep it simple, iterate.
So, with all of the above, here’s my advice:
Reinvent for insight. Reuse for impact.

不同观点：
• **支持重新发明轮子**：
   - **学习与理解**：重新发明轮子是深入理解技术概念的有效方法，尤其是从基础原理开始构建能够增强对技术的掌握（[megadragon9], [gfalcao], [richardjennings]）。
   - **创新与创造**：重新发明轮子可以带来新的视角和创新，甚至可能创造出比现有技术更好的解决方案（[boricj], [gfalcao] 的引用）。
   - **避免不必要的依赖**：通过重新发明轮子，可以避免引入过多的外部依赖，从而简化系统（[begueradj]）。

• **反对盲目重新发明轮子**：
   - **时间和资源限制**：在工作环境或创业公司中，重新发明轮子可能会浪费宝贵的时间和资源，尤其是在有现成且成熟的解决方案时（[mullingitover], [dustingetz], [kayodelycaon]）。
   - **生产环境中的风险**：除非重新发明的轮子在质量和功能上能超越现有方案，否则在生产环境中使用可能带来风险（[wcfrobert], [kayodelycaon]）。

• **中立或条件支持**：
   - **时机和目的**：重新发明轮子应根据具体情况决定，特别是在学习或需要定制解决方案时是有意义的，但在商业项目中需谨慎（[wcfrobert], [richardjennings]）。
